name: Diff Viewer
description: A Dioxus component that shows the differences between two texts, split or inline, with word-level detail on changed lines.
background:
1. react-diff-viewer serves only React apps; Dioxus apps have no equivalent diff viewer.
2. Its diffing and styling rest on JavaScript libraries (jsdiff, emotion) with no Rust counterparts, so the port rebuilds both on Rust foundations.
expected_users: Dioxus apps that show changes between two versions of text or code.

title: What changed
purpose: Ensures accurate change marking. Applies when reading or changing line and word comparison, or compare methods.
functional: Readers see which lines changed, and which words changed within them.

title: Where they are
purpose: Ensures readers stay oriented in long diffs. Applies when reading or changing folding, line numbering, highlighting, or line selection.
functional: Readers stay oriented in long diffs: unchanged lines fold away, and every line has a number.

title: How it fits the app
purpose: Ensures the viewer matches the app's look. Applies when reading or changing themes, style overrides, or title and line content rendering.
functional: Apps style the viewer, light or dark, and render line content their own way.

title: Compare methods
statement: Compare methods set the token size for inline diffs of modified lines.

title: Character comparison
statement: The viewer MUST compare modified lines character by character unless the consumer selects another compare method.

title: Word comparison
statement: The viewer MUST offer word comparison, with each whitespace run and each non-whitespace run as one token.

title: Line comparison
statement: The viewer MUST offer line comparison, with each modified line as one token.

title: Line changes
statement: Line changes pair the old and new texts line by line and mark what became of each line.

title: Line marking
summary: lines aligned as similar aligns them, each marked
statement: The viewer MUST mark each line as unchanged, removed, or added, aligning the two texts as `similar`'s line diff aligns them and comparing lines by their text without line terminators.

title: Modified lines
summary: removed lines pair in order with the added lines after them
statement: Where removed lines are immediately followed by added lines, the viewer MUST pair them in order as modified lines, and MUST show lines left without a partner as plain removals or additions.

title: Inline changes
summary: tokens changed within modified lines, on unless turned off
statement: Unless the consumer turns inline changes off, the viewer MUST mark within each modified line the tokens removed from the old line and the tokens added in the new line, using the selected compare method.

title: Trailing whitespace
summary: trailing whitespace of either text never shows as a change
statement: The viewer MUST ignore whitespace at the end of each text, so trailing blank lines never show as changes.

title: Line numbers
statement: Line numbers let readers locate each line within its own text.

title: Independent numbering
summary: old and new lines counted separately from the offset
statement: The viewer MUST number old-text lines and new-text lines independently, each starting at one more than the consumer's line offset, which defaults to 0.

title: Views
statement: Views lay the paired lines out side by side or in a single column.

title: Split view
summary: old left, new right, unless inline is chosen
statement: Unless the consumer selects the inline view, the viewer MUST show old lines on the left and new lines on the right, one pair per row.

title: Inline view
summary: one column, old text above new on modified lines
statement: In the inline view, the viewer MUST show lines in one column, with a modified line's old text directly above its new text, and each unchanged line once with both its old and new line numbers.

title: Change markers
statement: The viewer MUST mark removed lines with `-` and added lines with `+` in both views.

title: Hidden line numbers
statement: The viewer MUST show line numbers unless the consumer hides them.

title: Folding
statement: Folding hides unchanged lines far from any change while keeping them one action away.

title: Folded unchanged lines
summary: unchanged lines beyond the surrounding count fold away
statement: Unless the consumer turns folding off, the viewer MUST fold unchanged lines lying more than the surrounding-line count away from every change; that count defaults to 3.

title: Fold rows
summary: one row per fold, consumer may supply its content
statement: The viewer MUST show each fold as one row reading "Expand N lines ...", where N is the number of hidden lines, unless the consumer supplies the row's content, which the viewer MUST render from the hidden-line count and the old and new line numbers of the first hidden line.

title: Expanding folds
statement: Activating a fold row MUST reveal the lines it hides, and lines revealed by a fold row or from app code MUST stay revealed until an app returns every fold to folded, or the compared texts or the surrounding-line count change.
summary: revealed lines stay revealed until a reset or an input change

title: Where fold state lives
statement: The live diff an app holds MUST keep the expanded-fold state, so that no viewer keeps fold state of its own.
summary: the live diff keeps the fold state, not the viewer

title: Line selection
statement: Line selection lets apps point readers at specific lines and react when readers point back.

title: Highlighted lines
summary: lines listed by id are highlighted
statement: The viewer MUST highlight each line whose old-side or new-side line id the consumer lists, where a line id joins its side (`L` for old, `R` for new) and its line number with a hyphen, as in `L-20`.

title: Line number clicks
statement: When the consumer supplies a line-number click handler, the viewer MUST call it with the clicked line's id and the modifier keys held, each time a line number is clicked.
summary: handler gets the line id and held modifier keys

title: Content rendering
statement: Content rendering lets apps shape how titles and line text appear.

title: Column titles
statement: When the consumer supplies titles, the viewer MUST show the left title above the old column and the right title above the new column in the split view, and only the left title in the inline view; either title MAY be text or rendered content.

title: Custom line content
summary: consumer renderer shapes line text and inline tokens
statement: When the consumer supplies a content renderer, the viewer MUST render line text through it, including each inline-change token on modified lines, and MUST NOT call it for a side of a split row that has no line.

title: Themes
statement: Themes give the viewer light and dark appearances that fit the app and the reader.

title: Theme selection
summary: follows the reader's color-scheme preference unless the app chooses
statement: Unless the consumer selects light or dark, the viewer MUST follow the reader's light or dark color-scheme preference from the browser or platform.

title: Line ending changes
summary: differing terminators on paired lines are marked
statement: Where both lines of an unchanged or modified pair end with a line terminator and the two terminators differ, the viewer MUST mark that pair as carrying a line ending change, with each side's terminator.

title: Line ending chips
summary: each side's terminator shown as an escaped-text chip
statement: In both views, the viewer MUST show each side of a line ending change as a compact chip on that side's line, reading the terminator as escaped text: `\n`, `\r\n`, or `\r`; where the inline view shows an unchanged pair as one line, that line MUST show the old side's chip, then an arrow, then the new side's chip.

title: Chip and arrow color
summary: chips and the arrow contrast with the line backgrounds beneath them
statement: Each theme MUST color line ending chips, the line ending arrow, and whitespace chips so they contrast with every line background they appear on. The `react-diff-viewer` package renders none of these, so each theme names their colors rather than carrying them from the reference.

description: The crate root: its modules and the public names apps import.

Splits both texts into lines, aligns them through `similar`, and builds the paired entries: line marking, modified-line pairing, inline change tokens under each compare method, independent numbering, and the changed positions.
The consumer's input choices: compare method, whether to mark inline changes, and the line offset.
What the engine hands the component: paired line entries with each side's text and number, the change kind, inline tokens indexed into their line, and any line ending change.

title: Styling hooks
statement: The viewer MUST give itself, the title, each row, gutter, change marker, content cell, inline-change token, line ending chip, line ending arrow, whitespace chip, fold row, and the control expanding a fold row a stable class name naming its kind, plus a class for its split or inline view on the viewer itself, and for its change or highlight state elsewhere, if relevant, all prefixed with `dxdiff`, so that apps and themes can style the viewer without depending on its element structure or colliding with the app's own classes. A gutter that reports its clicks MUST additionally carry a class naming that, so the click affordance reaches only the gutters that answer a click.
summary: stable class per element kind, plus state classes and a clickable gutter

title: Trimmed line comparison
statement: The viewer MUST offer trimmed line comparison, with each modified line as one token, marked unchanged when the old and new lines differ only in leading or trailing whitespace.
summary: whole-line token ignoring leading and trailing whitespace

title: Leading or trailing whitespace changes
statement: Under trimmed line comparison, where the old and new lines of a modified pair differ in leading or trailing whitespace, the viewer MUST mark that pair as carrying a whitespace change.
summary: trimmed comparison still marks end-of-line whitespace edits

title: Whitespace chips
statement: In both views, the viewer MUST show a compact chip reading `WS` on each side's line of a pair carrying a whitespace change.
summary: WS chip on both sides of a whitespace change

title: Line ids from text
summary: text form reads back into a line id
statement: The viewer MUST let the consumer turn a line id's text form, as in `L-20` or `R-3`, back into a line id, and MUST report text in any other form as not a line id.

description: The component apps mount: its props, the engine call, fold state, and the viewer table with its titles.
The rows of both views: line rows with gutters, change markers, content, and chips, and fold rows.
Which rows a view shows: each paired line entry, or a fold row for a run of unchanged lines far from every change.
The expanded-fold state the viewer keeps, and the optional trigger an app uses to return every expanded fold to folded.
What the viewer hands the app's renderers and click handler: line content, hidden lines, and line-number clicks with held keys.
The `dxdiff` class names the viewer's markup carries for each element kind, view, and state.
Line ids: a line's side and number, written and read as `L-20` or `R-3`.

title: Rendered content identity
summary: rendered content stays with its line until a text changes
statement: The viewer MUST keep content from the consumer's renderers mounted with its line while the compared texts stay the same, including as folds expand, and MUST remount all such content when either text changes.

title: Theme palettes
statement: The viewer MUST color every element it renders from one named set of colors per theme, and the light and dark sets MUST carry the colors the `react-diff-viewer` package uses for the same elements.
summary: one named color set per theme, carrying the reference colors

title: Style delivery
statement: The viewer MUST render its own styles into the document, so that an app mounting it adds no stylesheet of its own.
summary: the viewer brings its own styles; the app adds none

title: Palette override
statement: An app MUST be able to restyle the viewer, wholly or one mounted viewer at a time, using only its own CSS.
summary: app CSS alone restyles the viewer, everywhere or one at a time

title: Named colors
statement: The viewer MUST read every theme color from a `dxdiff`-prefixed custom property, and MUST declare each property's default at the document root, so that an app's assignment on any ancestor takes effect for a viewer following the reader's color-scheme preference. A viewer given an explicit theme MAY carry that theme's values on its own element, in which case an app restyles it with rules reaching the viewer element or below.
summary: colors read from dxdiff custom properties defaulted at the root

title: Yielding rules
statement: The viewer's own style rules MUST yield to an app's rules for the same element whatever their specificity, so that an app never needs `!important` to restyle the viewer.
summary: the viewer's rules lose to the app's, whatever the specificity

title: Line numbers under the pointer
summary: a row's numbers read fully while the pointer is over it
statement: The viewer MUST read a row's line numbers at full strength while the pointer is over that row, and at reduced strength otherwise, whether or not the viewer reports line-number clicks. At full strength each number MUST reach a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 against every gutter background it can appear on.

title: Row under the pointer
summary: the hovered row tints without hiding its change colors
statement: The viewer MUST tint the row under the pointer so a reader can follow one line across the viewer, and the tint MUST lie over each line's own change color rather than replace it. The `react-diff-viewer` package tints no row, so each theme names the tint rather than carrying it from the reference.

title: Driving it from code
purpose: Ensures an app can read a mounted viewer and open its folds from its own code. Applies when reading or changing what the crate reports about a diff's changes and hidden lines, or the actions that open folds and return them to folded.
functional: Apps ask a mounted diff where its changes are and which lines are hidden, and open folds from their own code.

title: The live diff
statement: An app holds a diff of two texts as live state, and the viewer renders that state rather than computing its own.

title: Building a live diff
statement: The crate MUST let an app build a live diff from an old and a new text alone, and MUST offer a second form taking one options value carrying the compare method, whether inline changes are marked, the line offset, whether unchanged lines fold, and how many unchanged lines surround each change, every field defaulted.
summary: two texts alone, or texts with one fully defaulted options value

title: Rendering a live diff
statement: The viewer MUST take a live diff as its only data prop, and MUST keep as its own props the view, the theme, line-number visibility, highlighted lines, the content and fold-row renderers, the line-number click handler, and the titles.
summary: the live diff is the viewer's only data prop

title: One plan per live diff
statement: Viewers rendering the same live diff MUST show the same rows, so that a fold opened through that live diff opens in every one of them.
summary: viewers over one live diff share its row plan

title: Reading a diff
statement: A live diff answers where its changes are and which lines its folds hide, in the line numbers an app already sees on screen.

title: Where the changes are
statement: A live diff MUST report its changes in document order, each as one run of consecutive changed lines with the old-side and new-side line numbers that run spans. The lines it counts as changed MUST be the ones folding measures its surrounding-line count from.
summary: changes as runs, in each side's line numbers

title: Which lines are hidden
statement: A live diff MUST report which lines its folds hide at the moment it is asked, each hidden run with the old-side and new-side line numbers that run spans, so that a fold a reader has already expanded is reported as hidden no longer.
summary: hidden runs, current as of the asking

title: Opening and refolding
statement: An app opens folds through the live diff by naming a line, and returns them all to folded, never naming a fold itself.

title: Expanding at a line
statement: A live diff MUST reveal the whole run of hidden lines holding a line an app names by its line id, and MUST leave the shown lines unchanged when the named line is not hidden.
summary: name a hidden line, get its whole run back

title: Expanding everything
statement: A live diff MUST reveal every line its folds hide, in one action.
summary: one action opens every fold

title: Resetting folds
statement: A live diff MUST return every expanded fold to folded, in one action.
summary: one action refolds everything
